title: David Choe's Controversial Opinion on Star Wars
summary: A 1:56 official-channel two-person excerpt about Asian representation in Star Wars. The speaker recalls criticizing Rian Johnson, describes the franchise he inherited as white, then traces what he sees as Asian-coded caricature across the Trade Federation, Rogue One’s blind martial-artist role and The Last Jedi’s student-body/glee-club/tattletale characterization. He connects those examples to scarcity: when Asian people appear rarely in television and film, Bruce Lee, Long Duk Dong and Gung Ho-style portrayals can become generalized identities. Every racial term, performed accent, sexuality speculation, insult and profanity mask remains uncensored. The closing “keep Star Wars white” is preserved only with the complete critique as a provocative reversal joke, not a literal archive conclusion. Work/character context is repaired without asserting canon sexuality or film approval. Auto captions do not publisher-label either participant; zero named turns ship.
